title: Residency & retention bundles with subprocessor transparency pilot
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: design and run a pilot that packages data locality and extended retention as discrete, billable bundles while providing automated subprocessor disclosure and an SCC-ready contract path. The pilot should validate price sensitivity for (a) control-plane vs data-plane separation, (b) 30/90/365 day retention tiers, and (c) a paid subprocessor attestation add-on. Deliverables include SKU definitions, console/UI flow for selection, API surface flags, a legal addendum template (SCC insertion + audit checklist), and a small closed pilot with 3 enterprise customers to measure conversion and revenue uplift.
acceptance_criteria: Three pricing SKUs defined and documented (Local-30, Local-90, Local-365) with clear feature bullets
Console and API residency/retention selection implemented behind feature-flag for pilots
Legal addendum draft that supports auto-insertion of SCCs and includes subprocessor attestation language
Pilot contracts executed with 3 enterprise customers and handoff notes to Sales Ops
Telemetry collecting selection rate, conversion to paid plan, average deal size delta, and support tickets related to residency/retention
steps: 1) Align scope with Legal on minimum acceptable SCC insertion flow and required attestation fields
2) Sketch Console and API flows with Design and get PM/Engineering sign-off
3) Implement backend flags and billing SKU plumbing (billing, metering tags) behind a pilot feature flag
4) Create Sales playbook + contract addendum template and run internal training session
5) Recruit 3 pilot customers (target: current mid-market accounts with residency asks) and negotiate short SOWs
6) Run pilot for 8 weeks, capture telemetry and qualitative feedback, iterate on UI/contract language
7) Analyze results and present recommendation: ship, iterate, or cancel
success_metrics: Pilot conversion rate >= 20% of trial customers selecting a paid residency bundle
Average deal size uplift >= 12% for accounts that purchase residency/retention bundles
Time-to-contract (with SCC addendum) <= 30 days for pilot customers
Number of security/legal escalations <= 1 per pilot customer
Positive NPS/comments from pilot contacts around clarity of subprocessor list and retention terms
risks: Legal review could significantly delay the addendum language or require bespoke contract commitments
Engineering capacity constrained by Dedicated/private roadmap leading to longer implementation time
Pricing miscalculation: too high leads to low uptake; too low reduces ARR upside
Operational burden for support and Sales Ops to manage custom retention requests
Complexity of ensuring true regional data residency across cloud providers for pilot customers
